Documentation → Releases → 1.0

SATOM 1.0

The first production release, with DNS record management, an alert engine, certificate auto-renewal, configuration drift detection, safer restores and a Linux installer.

👤 ForViewerOperatorAdministratorAdvanced user

  • What's new
  • DNS records management (IPAM/DDI)

Released: 2026-07-14 · All releases

In short#

The first production release. It adds:

  • DNS record management
  • an alert engine with email delivery
  • automatic certificate renewal
  • detection of configuration drift
  • health snapshots around upgrades and restores
  • a safer, gated way to restore a device's configuration

It is also the first release with a Linux installer and offline bundles.

What's new#

DNS records management (IPAM/DDI)#

The DNS & LB lookup tool has a new +DNS Records section. You can create, view, edit and delete DNS records there. The records live in your IPAM system: EfficientIP SOLIDserver, phpIPAM or NetBox.

Alert engine#

SATOM sends alerts in the console and by email for four situations:

  • certificates about to expire
  • the git copy of the configurations drifting from the main repository
  • devices that cannot be reached
  • backups that are out of date

Administrators set the thresholds.

Certificate auto-renewal#

A nightly renewal job can either only alert (the default) or automatically fetch the renewed certificate from the edge.

Configuration drift detection#

SATOM compares each device's configuration with the copy in the configuration source of truth (kept in git) and reports differences. Values that change on their own all the time are ignored, so you see real changes only.

Safer upgrades and restores#

  • Health snapshots are taken before and after an upgrade or restore, so you can compare them.
  • Gated restores. Restoring a device's configuration is first tried as a small test and goes ahead only if it passes.

Firmware manifest#

The list of firmware images is rebuilt automatically whenever you upload, pull or delete an image.

Production releases#

  • A Linux installer, with offline bundles for Debian and RHEL.
  • Support for the common package managers.
  • A public website.
  • Published release packages.

Fixed#

  • Upgrade event times are now shown in your local time instead of UTC.
